section_summary: This section finishes translations of Japanese laws and regulations protecting military material secrets, then presents an education rescript and a law placing religious bodies under state supervision. It turns to wartime controls on foreigners’ property and financial transactions, ending with a list of designated countries and the beginning of a general license.

subfiles.title: Law for Safeguarding Secrets of Military Material Resources of Japan
subfiles.about: The concluding articles define protected military information, secrecy measures, offenses and penalties.
subfiles.summary: The law covers military transport, communications, research and related facilities. It authorizes concealment and access restrictions, provides compensation for required measures, and penalizes disclosure or collection of secrets. Its final provisions address permission to disclose secrets and administration in Chosen, Taiwan and Karafuto.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Enforcement of the Law for Safeguarding Secrets of Military Material Resources of Japan
subfiles.about: Imperial Ordinance No. 413 sets procedures for designating, marking, concealing and disclosing military material secrets.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance assigns consultation duties among the War and Navy ministers and other authorities, including colonial administrators. It governs secrecy markings, restricted access, official credentials, compensation claims and permissions to disclose protected material.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Enforcement of the Law of Safeguarding Secrets of Military Material Resources of Japan
subfiles.doc_type: War and Navy ministries ordinance, translation
subfiles.about: Ordinance No. 3 specifies secrecy procedures and lists military resources and production data subject to protection.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance details marking, concealment, entry permits, credentials, inspections, compensation and disclosure applications. Its appended list identifies protected production and capacity figures, imports, stockpiles, equipment, skilled personnel, vehicles, horses and railway capacity. The listed materials include metals, fuels, aircraft and weapons, with coverage extending to Japanese territories and named import ports.

subfiles.title: VI. Educational Religions and Social Controls: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: The note introduces education ideology and state control of Christian churches.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the education rescript and the 1939 Religious Body Law.

subfiles.title: Imperial Rescript on Education
subfiles.about: The rescript instructs subjects in loyalty, filial duty, learning, public service and defense of the imperial throne.
subfiles.summary: The rescript presents moral duties and loyalty to the imperial throne as the basis of education.

subfiles.title: The Religious Body Law of Japan
subfiles.about: Law No. 77 establishes government approval, registration and supervision of religious bodies and their property.
subfiles.summary: The law regulates the founding, incorporation, leadership, merger and dissolution of Shinto, Buddhist, Christian and other religious bodies. It requires approval for many organizational and property decisions and gives officials power to restrict activities deemed contrary to public order or subjects’ duties. It also sets reporting requirements, tax provisions, penalties, appeals and transitional rules for existing institutions.

subfiles.title: VII. Alien Property and Business Transactions: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: The note introduces Japan’s controls on designated foreigners’ transactions and subsequent enemy property measures.
subfiles.summary: Places the July 1941 transaction ordinance and December 1941 enemy assets law in context.

subfiles.title: Regulations for Control of Transactions Concerning Foreigners
subfiles.about: Ordinance No. 46 requires permission and reports for designated foreigners’ property and financial transactions.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines designated countries, nationals, affiliated entities and residents. It restricts property transfers, deposits, loans, currency dealings, business interests and transactions undertaken for designated foreigners, with specified exceptions and permission procedures. It requires initial and monthly reports on property, obligations and investments, and links its rules to the Foreign Exchange Control Law.

subfiles.title: List of Countries Designated by Minister of Finance Under Ordinance No. 46
subfiles.about: Notifications dated July 28–August 2, 1941 name countries and territories subject to the transaction controls.
subfiles.summary: Lists the United States, British, Dutch and other countries and territories designated under Ordinance No. 46.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 284, Ministry of Finance: General License No. 1
subfiles.doc_type: official gazette notification and general license
subfiles.about: The license provides an exception for specified transactions involving bank bills accepted before July 26, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Begins a general license covering specified clearing transactions involving banks of designated foreign countries; the text continues beyond this section.
